analysis: The PR only touches documentation: docs/developer/test.md adds a 'Prompt Preparation And Admission' section (head lines 63-81) and docs/provider/cli-reference.md adds a benchmark table row for `--prompt-prep` (head line 527). No source code, configuration, cryptographic, authorization, or attestation behavior changes in the supplied evidence, so none of the canonical assets or boundaries (TB-002, TB-003, TB-007, TB-009, TB-011, T-041) has a changed control. The documented tests use synthetic tokenizers with no download, the benchmark is CPU-only and loads only the tokenizer, and it needs no model weights, credentials or coordinator access. The documented `PROMPT_TOKEN_CACHE_MODEL_DIRS` variable only points to local directories. T-041 covers the encrypted SSD prefix cache. The new docs mention a 'PromptTokenCache' and 'cached ... token IDs', which is a prompt-preparation cache. Its scoping and tenant isolation cannot be assessed from the supplied evidence, because the underlying implementation (PromptTokenCache, InboundChatRequestDecode, PromptPreparationBenchmark.swift) is not in this batch. If the real code adds a token-ID cache shared across consumers, it could add a new cross-tenant timing or retention surface outside T-041, so the threat model would need updating. The docs state only that results are checked for equality with the unchanged path. The remaining integration question is whether the companion source change in this PR, if any, keeps any prompt-token cache scoped per request or bounded in memory. The `docs/provider/cli-reference.md` base text excerpt ends at line 418, but the patch is complete, so no further patch content is missing. No findings are raised from documentation alone.
